I have 60 mu, and because my family has some people working off-farm, I will keep the farm organized around the crops I know best and the work rhythm I can actually handle. I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize system because that is the backbone of my farm and gives me steady grain output across the year. I will leave a smaller part for cotton because cotton can still bring cash, but it needs more spraying and more field attention, so I do not want to put too much of my land into it. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect wheat at key stages, support maize after summer sowing, and keep cotton from suffering in dry periods. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize and cotton seed because I want stable emergence, stronger growth, and better yield from the same land. For tillage, I will keep wheat on rotary tillage, put maize mostly under no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time and catch the sowing window, and use plough tillage for cotton land so the soil is looser at planting. I will not push fertilizer to extremes; I will use solid but manageable input levels so I can control cost and still aim for dependable yields. My plan is to put labor and water first where they matter most, keep the grain system stable, and use cotton as a smaller cash crop rather than the main crop.
